title: Genesis IQ
subtitle: How well do you know the book of beginnings?

questions.text: On which day did God create the sun, moon, and stars?

options.explanation: The first day brought light, but the sun, moon, and stars came later.
The third day brought dry land and vegetation.
Genesis 1:14-19 says, "And God made two great lights... the stars also." That's day four.
Day six brought land animals and mankind.

questions.text: What was the name of the garden God placed Adam in?

options.explanation: Gethsemane shows up in the New Testament. It's the garden where Jesus prayed before the cross.
Genesis 2:8 puts it plainly: "And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden."
Goshen was the region in Egypt where Israel settled under Joseph.
Shiloh was a later worship site in Israel, not the original garden.
Seth was the son Adam and Eve had after Abel's death.
Lamech was a later descendant of Cain who also boasted of killing a man.
In Genesis 4:8, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and slew him.
Enoch was a righteous man who "walked with God," not a murderer.

questions.text: How old was Noah when the flood came on the earth?

options.explanation: Noah was 500 when he began having sons (Genesis 5:32).
Genesis 7:6 says, "Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was upon the earth."
Noah lived to 950 (Genesis 9:29), but the flood came at 600.
That was the total length of Noah's life, not his age at the flood.

questions.text: What did God use to set in the cloud as a sign of His covenant with Noah?

options.explanation: Stars are signs elsewhere in Scripture, but not the rainbow covenant.
Genesis 9:13 says, "I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant."
The dove brought back an olive leaf, but the covenant sign was the bow.
The dove returned with an olive leaf to signal the waters had gone down, but that wasn't the covenant sign.

questions.text: What city did the people build with a tower that God confused with many languages?

options.explanation: Nineveh was the Assyrian capital where Jonah preached, not the tower city.
Genesis 11:9 says, "Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth."
Sodom was destroyed by fire, not language confusion.
Ur was Abraham's homeland, not the tower city.

questions.text: What was Abraham's name before God changed it?

options.explanation: Genesis 17:5 says, "Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee."
Aram was a region/people in the ancient Near East, not Abraham's prior name.
Eber was an ancestor, not Abraham's earlier name.
Adam was the first man, generations before Abraham.

questions.text: Sarah laughed when she heard she would bear a son. What did God name the child?

options.explanation: Ishmael was Abraham's son by Hagar, not Sarah's son.
Genesis 21:3 says, "And Abraham called the name of his son... Isaac." Fittingly, the name means "laughter."
Jacob was Isaac's son and Sarah's grandson.
Esau was Isaac's son, not Sarah's son.

questions.text: On what mountain did Abraham nearly sacrifice Isaac?

options.explanation: Mount Sinai is where Moses received the Law much later.
Mount Carmel is where Elijah confronted the prophets of Baal.
Genesis 22:2 says, "Get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains."
Mount Hermon is in northern Israel, associated with the Transfiguration in some traditions.

questions.text: What did Esau sell to Jacob for a bowl of stew?

options.explanation: Esau was a hunter, but the trade wasn't for a weapon.
The trade wasn't for property.
Genesis 25:33 puts it bluntly: "And he sold his birthright unto Jacob."
Esau kept his name; what he sold was his birthright as firstborn.

questions.text: What did Jacob see in his dream at Bethel?

options.explanation: The burning bush was Moses' encounter centuries later.
Genesis 28:12 says, "And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven."
Chariot visions belong to Zechariah and other prophets.
Scroll visions belong to Ezekiel and Revelation.

questions.text: After wrestling all night with the angel, what was Jacob's new name?

options.explanation: Genesis 32:28 says, "Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed."
Judah was one of Jacob's sons, not his new name.
Bethel was the place where Jacob had his ladder dream.
Peniel was the name Jacob gave the place of the wrestling, since he said "I have seen God face to face." His own new name, though, was Israel.

questions.text: How many sons did Jacob have who became the tribes of Israel?

options.explanation: Joseph and Benjamin would be missing from a list of ten.
Genesis 35:22-26 lists Jacob's twelve sons, the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Leah had six sons of her own, but Jacob fathered twelve total.
Jacob had twelve sons. The tribe count sometimes lists Joseph's two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, separately, but the sons themselves number twelve.

questions.text: Why did Joseph's brothers sell him into slavery?

options.explanation: Joseph didn't steal anything; his brothers acted out of jealousy.

options.text: They were jealous of his coat and his dreams
options.explanation: In Genesis 37:3-11, Joseph's coat of many colors and his dreams of his brothers bowing made them envy him.
Joseph was the victim, not the betrayer.
Jacob was devastated when he believed Joseph was dead; he never sanctioned this.

questions.text: How does the book of Genesis end?

options.text: With Israel crossing the Red Sea
options.explanation: The Red Sea crossing is in Exodus 14.
Abraham's death is in Genesis 25, well before the end.
Genesis 50:26 closes the book: "So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt."
Moses' birth is in Exodus 2.

gradeBands.message: Few know Genesis like you do.
